title: MutationReport
description: v0.1. Mutation testing of a certified Java translation: how strong is the verification itself? Small realistic faults (a flipped comparison, a changed rounding mode, a dropped truncation, ...) are seeded into a COPY of the Java, and each mutant is run through the same differential harness on the same held-out inputs. A killed mutant means the inputs would have detected that mistake. A surviving mutant is a COVERAGE QUESTION (no input exercised the difference, or the change is harmless in a way the cheap rules cannot see), not automatically a defect and not a confidence score. No model is involved: operators, selection and extra inputs are deterministic. The certified Java is never modified.

status.description: ok: mutants were run. unsupported: the sample shape is not covered (see reason). baseline-failed: the unmutated Java did not match the original on these inputs, so mutants cannot be judged.

reason.description: Why status is not ok, in plain words

seed.description: Selection of mutants and extra inputs is a pure function of this seed and the Java source

initial.description: Number of inputs the certified verification used (the ones every mutant is first run on)

generated.description: Mutants the operators could place in the Java, before the cap

run.description: Mutants selected and processed (at most caps.maxMutants)

survived.description: Initial inputs did NOT detect the fault (some may be killed later by extra inputs, see augmented)

equivalentSuspected.description: Flagged by a cheap deterministic rule only (identical normalised bytecode); never by a model

timeout.description: The mutant exceeded its time limit; a certification run would also have failed on it, so it counts as detected

error.description: The harness failed on this mutant (not the mutant's fault); excluded from the score

notRun.description: Selected but not processed because the wall-clock cap was reached

score.description: (killed + timeout) / (killed + timeout + survived), over mutants that compiled and are not equivalent-suspected, by the INITIAL inputs only. null when that denominator is 0. A measure of how many seeded faults the inputs detected, not a probability that the translation is correct.

operator.description: e.g. relational-swap, arithmetic-swap, rounding-mode, remove-truncation, scale-off-by-one, boundary-constant, negate-condition, loop-bound, remove-else, string-compare, pad-char

original.description: The source text that was replaced (trimmed, at most 200 characters)

mutated.description: What it was replaced with (trimmed, at most 200 characters)

killedBy.description: Id of the first input that detected it, or stdout / exit-code

augmentedOutcome.description: Only on mutants that survived the initial inputs: result of re-running them on the extra inputs

note.description: Rule that flagged equivalent-suspected, compiler message of a not-compiled mutant, or the harness error (short)

augmented.description: Extra inputs generated deterministically (boundary emphasis, duplicated and blank keys, neighbours of existing values), shared by all survivors; only survivors are re-run on them.

notes.description: Honest labels: a surviving mutant is a coverage question, not automatically a defect; equivalent-suspected is a cheap rule, not a proof; the operators are a sample of realistic faults, not all faults.
